mutations.intent: With create_consumer=false and a server-side ack policy of none, the runtime still acks and sets Mesh-Deadline.
backoff with as many entries as max_deliver is accepted at New.
Start fails on a server without JetStream instead of passing the boot check.
Expiry of request_timeout is reported as context.DeadlineExceeded instead of ErrTimeout.
The time left is the later of request_timeout and the context deadline, so Mesh-Timeout overstates it.
The consumer is created without the subscriber's ack_wait.
The consumer is created without max_deliver, so a failing message is delivered without limit.
Client.Stream reads the wrong key, so it finds no stream for a target that names one.
create_consumer=false on a none subscriber is accepted at New instead of returning ErrBadConfig.
A delivery's deadline uses the next backoff entry instead of its own.
A subscriber that sets no max_deliver gets 4 deliveries instead of the documented 5.
ack_policy double acks without waiting for confirmation, and explicit waits.
An endpoint handler's context no longer carries the request's deadline.
ConsumerGroup none becomes a queue group named "none" instead of a plain subscription.
A HandlerError comes back with empty Text instead of the handler's message.
A handler no longer sees Nats-Msg-Id copied into Mesh-Message-Id.
Per-call options and endpoint or subscriber metadata no longer override the target's settings.
Mesh-Nats-Num-Pending carries the delivery count instead of the pending count.
A set nak_delay is ignored, so a failed message is sent again right away.
nak_delay is read from ack_wait, so a set nak_delay has no effect.
A named group's consumer takes the server's inactive threshold instead of 7 days.
An ordered consumer defaults to a 7-day inactive threshold instead of 5 minutes.
Mesh-Message-Id no longer sets Nats-Msg-Id on sent messages, so streams don't drop duplicates.
A JetStream publish no longer expects the named stream, so a subject stored by another stream succeeds.
